reviews.review: Fun game, Good mechanics, Runs great on Linux
Pretty amazing game. Fun and addicting although its age shows.

I'll be honest, after a few particularly bad runs I was about to give it a negative review - such are the depths of the salt mines I found myself in. But it's not that the game is bad; the huge variety of items can be quite crippling, however, if you chose to play the regular randomized way. But I'm getting ahead of myself.

Risk of Rain is a 2-D sidescrolling rogue-like Gun 'n Run where you pick one of twelve characters (though all but the starting class, the Commando, need to be unlocked) that has you killing everything that isn't you - or your allies (...well, you may sometimes CAUSE their death but no blood on your hands, eh?) - while you search for the teleporter located somewhere on each of the several stages. Along the way you'll find chests, shrines and store-like thingymajigs that allow you to aquire one of RoR's sizeable item pool's equipments in exchange for money you loot off of the local fauna. These items usually buff a stat like Speed, Health Regen, or similar, but can also add new effects or on-hit/on-kill abilities.

Regarding the characters, each comes with a basic attack that is fairly spam-able and three skills with differing cooldowns. They managed to give each class a unique feel, as good as they can - admittedly, there are only so many spins you can take on a melee-type. Some of them focus on mobility, others on Damage over Time, and some are more jack-of-all-trades. As you kill more and more monsters you will level up, gaining a few hp and a slight damage boost. Putting regular old bullets will only get you so far, though, so it is imperative that you collect as many items as quickly as you can, because the difficulty increases every few minutes (how quickly it increases depends on your basic difficulty chosen).

This is where some runs can quickly turn you into a lump of rocksalt, though. Of course, being a rogue-like it was to be expected that you won't always get the items you want, but it feels like there is a selection of equipment that seems almost prerequisite for success whereas others can hardly make a difference. Or they'll just be of no use for your chosen class - sure, dealing damage on contact sounds pretty swell for melee, but if I'm playing ranged I don't necessarily want to be in mauling range of a swarm of enemies. It can get really tiresome if you repeatedly fail to make it past the third stage because Random Number Jesus didn't deign to give you Lifesteal or any kind of mobility boost. Fortunately there is an Artifact - one of a few hidden items that costumize your playthrough - which turns random items into a sort of "lootbox", allowing you to pick an item of your own choosing. Admittedly, it takes away some of the challenge, but I rather enjoy myself and take solace that, in case I die, it was of my own lack of skill and not of my poor choice in appropriate equipment.

I can highly recommend this game to anyone who likes side-scrolling shooters, even at full price. On the other hand, if you're not a big fan of random influence in your entertainment, I'd still tell you to give it a shot when it's on sale.
